title: Import-boundary check
responsibility: Statically prove, without executing the application, that every planning-content read goes through the reader inside a `<Suspense>` boundary and that no module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`. Detect bypass paths rather than only direct violations.
notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ IT EXISTS BECAUSE TESTING CANNOT DO THIS. AST-0022 measured that a non-compliant read is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route, so every behavioural freshness check passes on a codebase that breaks the contract — until the compliant sibling moves, and then every read on that route silently reverts to build-time content. A test that passes on broken code is worse than no test, because it is also a claim that the code was checked. ⚠️ TWO EDGES, ONE GRAPH: reads outside the abstraction, and `app/**` importing `lib/**` outside `app/server/`. The adapter boundary has the same property — an app module importing `lib/` directly behaves identically until someone renders it from a client component. ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS NOT FIXED HERE: a lint rule, a module-boundary constraint, a generated accessor or a build-step scan would each satisfy it. What is fixed is that it runs without executing the application. ⚠️ HALF BUILT 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0006. The `app/server` → `lib/` import boundary is analysed, falsified and wired into `npm run lint:shell` and the test suite. ACC-0023 passes. ⚠️ ACC-0021, ACC-0022 AND ACC-0024 REMAIN `not-evaluated`. The planning-read and `<Suspense>` confinement half is TSK-0015, and ACC-0024 asks for the FULL violation set with failing fixtures — marking it now would claim a pair on the strength of one half. ⚠️ SCOPE IS EVERY MODULE UNDER `app/`, NOT ONLY WHAT A ROUTE REACHES, and that was a corrected defect rather than an initial choice. Reachability-scoped, the check walked two files and reported the project clean while never looking at the reader or either adapter. Reachability now supplies only the chain that explains a violation. ⚠️ ONE EXCLUSION, DECLARED IN `shellBoundaryConfig`: `app/server.mjs`, the walking skeleton DEC-0017 preserves. Excluding it by name makes a second exclusion a visible act; excluding it by unreachability would have silently excluded most of the shell. ⚠️ COMPLETED 2026-08-28 BY TSK-0015. All four of its criteria now pass. Both halves run from one command, `npm run lint:shell`, and from the test suite. ⚠️ SIX DETECTORS ACROSS THE TWO HALVES, EACH WITH A FIXTURE THAT FIRES IT, and a test that counts them — so a detector added later without a control fails the suite rather than joining it quietly. Every one was also falsified against a temporary violation in the real application, because a fixture only proves a detector works on a fixture. ⚠️ IT REFUSES RATHER THAN REPORTING CLEAN in three cases that would otherwise look like success: no route entry points, a designated reader that does not exist, and a computed dynamic import it cannot resolve. Each of those would have produced a green result from a check that examined nothing. ⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, recorded rather than implied: a computed specifier; a component rendered through a variable or passed as a prop rather than by name; and a path alias, since only relative specifiers are resolved and none is configured today.
